title: 5. Phase 3 — Containment, Eradication, Recovery
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L20: Incident Response: 5. Phase 3 — Containment, Eradication, Recovery.

items: Short-term containment — stop the bleeding now (isolate host, disable account, block IP at firewall)
Long-term containment — sustainable hold while you investigate (network segmentation, hardened access control)

blocks.text: Critical rule — Evidence first: When safe to do so, preserve evidence before containment. Memory forensics is impossible after a power-off. Disk evidence is destroyed by reimaging.

Containment trade-off: isolate (loud, attacker knows) vs monitor (silent, learn TTPs but more risk). For confirmed ransomware → isolate immediately. For suspected APT reconnaissance → carefully monitor with controlled deception, if you have the maturity.

items: Remove malware from every affected system (prefer rebuild from clean image over manual cleanup — you can never be 100% sure malware is gone)
Patch the vulnerability that enabled initial access
Reset credentials — every potentially-compromised account, including service accounts and tokens
Audit accounts for attacker-created persistence (new admin accounts, scheduled tasks, registry Run keys, web shells)
Restore from clean backup — verify backup integrity before restore
Staged return to production — validate one system before bringing the whole environment back
Enhanced monitoring for 30 days — attackers often have multiple footholds; reinfection within weeks is common

blocks.text: `` ☐ Backup verified clean (offline / immutable) ☐ Vulnerability patched ☐ Credentials rotated (including service accounts) ☐ Persistence mechanisms removed ☐ EDR re-deployed and reporting ☐ Enhanced monitoring active for 30 days ``
